title: $100 Billion Investment Push As India Accelerates India-EFTA Trade Pact Implementation
text:
News Brief
Arjun Brij
Jan 08, 2026 | Updated 10:12 AM GMT+5:30

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal began 2026 with a diplomatic outreach to Liechtenstein, underscoring India’s intent to swiftly translate the India–EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA) into tangible trade, investment and manufacturing outcomes.
The official visit on 7 January marked the first ministerial engagement of the year and carried clear signals of India’s expanding global economic ambition.
During the visit, Goyal met H.S.H. Hereditary Prince Alois von und zu Liechtenstein at Vaduz Castle and held discussions with Prime Minister Brigitte Haas and Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sabine Monauni.
His engagements also included interactions with the business community, an interview with ORF, and a visit to Hilti AG, where he discussed opportunities for deeper industrial collaboration.
The Minister highlighted Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s broader economic vision, recalling his observation that “The world is seeing India with a ray of hope amidst uncertainty”.
Goyal noted that this optimism reflects India’s approach to partnerships that deliver practical outcomes for businesses, MSMEs, farmers and local communities.
TEPA, India’s first free trade agreement with the European Free Trade Association—comprising Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland—marks a shift towards a higher-quality economic relationship.
Goyal underlined that India’s manufacturing ecosystem is increasingly defined by scale, competitiveness and reliability, aligning with the goals of “Make in India” and “Make for the World”.
In his meetings, the Minister positioned India as a stable and scalable destination for long-term investment, citing its status as the world’s fourth-largest economy with an estimated GDP of USD 4.13 trillion in 2025.
He emphasised that India’s market size, reform momentum and infrastructure push can complement Liechtenstein’s strengths in specialised manufacturing, innovation and financial services.
At Hilti AG, Goyal encouraged stronger industry-to-industry ties, greater supplier integration including MSMEs, and an expanded role for India-based manufacturing in global value chains.
He invited EFTA companies to leverage TEPA to deepen their presence in India and participate in its growth story.
The visit concluded with a call to intensify India–Liechtenstein and broader India–EFTA engagement, with TEPA carrying an agreed ambition to facilitate USD 100 billion in investments and support the creation of one million direct jobs.
